sections.h2: Listing or cash sale in Durham
sections.html:
A listing aims for the highest price. A cash sale aims for speed and a shorter to-do list. Durham owners with an inherited, tenant-occupied or worn-out house often collect both numbers before they choose.

  • Agent listing: a good match when the house shows well and you can sit through inspections and a buyer's loan underwriting.
  • Sale by owner: workable if you can set a price and handle the contract yourself.
  • Cash purchase: useful when repairs, tenants, probate or a firm date make a long listing impractical.

The deed is filed in Durham County, and state law ranks competing conveyances by the order in which each was registered. That is one reason your closing attorney files promptly after funds move.

Durham had an estimated 305,561 residents in mid-2025, up from 283,506 in 2020 and 228,330 in 2010. Only 52.3 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, so nearly half of households rent. A Durham house may well sell with a tenant inside, and then the lease becomes a sale document. A landlord can bid as readily as a family can.

Values now in force date from January 1, 2025, and the next county reappraisal is set for January 1, 2029. State law requires every county to reappraise within eight years, though commissioners can pull the date forward by resolution. Durham shortened its cycle because a long gap in a fast-growing place produces large, unpredictable swings.

Between reappraisals a parcel's value can still change through new construction, rezoning or a split. The county then applies the last cycle's rates. A house built in 2026 on land that was vacant in 2025 is appraised at January 1, 2025 prices.

  • The office values property at full fair market value as of the effective date.
  • Appraising and taxing are separate steps, and each jurisdiction picks its own rate.
  • Measurements are taken from the outside, so the county's square footage can differ from a fee appraisal.

Buying a new build? Have the closing attorney estimate tax from the price. You get a rough figure, not the bill itself.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Durham County value
sections.html:
File in the county's Tax Help portal, which is the method the county recommends, or on a paper form. Either way, file before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. A change-of-value notice instead opens a window of 30 days. The county's call center, 919-560-0300, can mail you a form.

The adjournment date is announced each year in the Durham Herald-Sun and on the county website, so follow the current notice. A review runs 30 to 120 days. Affordability and the size of a bill increase are not grounds for a change.

  • Bring comparable sales. For the 2025 cycle the county looked at 2023 and 2024 sales and excluded related-party deals, foreclosures, short sales and auctions.
  • A fee appraisal or closing statement from near the effective date can help, though one sale may not show the typical price.
  • Relief is prospective: G.S. 105-287 says a lowered value is not retroactive.

Five residents sit on the board, each named by a different county commissioner. You may attend, but the board will rule on your papers if you cannot. Beyond the board sits the state Property Tax Commission, which you reach within a month of the board's mailed decision.

sections.h2: Who can file for an heir or a company
sections.html:
For a person's home, the owner, a North Carolina attorney or a holder of power of attorney may file. Only the owner or a lawyer may argue at the hearing, because the county treats its board as quasi-judicial and advocacy there can amount to practicing law.

Entities have a narrower list: a lawyer, an officer, an LLC manager, an authorized W-2 employee, or an owner holding at least a quarter of the company. All but the lawyer file a non-attorney representative form, and an agent under power of attorney may not file for an entity.

Selling an inherited house? Check who held title on January 1, because the county fixes ownership annually on that date. Forward any notice that reaches you after a sale to the new owner.

Three state programs exist, and each owner picks a single one. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor.

  • Older or disabled owners: an exclusion of at least $25,000, tied to a 2026 income cap the state form prints as $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 of value excluded, with no age or income cap on the form.
  • Circuit breaker: tax is held to a share of income, and the difference is deferred as a lien.

The county's FAQ also describes present-use treatment for farmland and woodland. Agriculture needs a 10 acre tract in production, horticulture needs 5 acres, and forestry needs 20 acres, with a $1,000 average gross income test over three years for the first two.

sections.h2: Deed tax and recording costs for a Durham seller
sections.html:
Sellers owe deed excise tax at the Register of Deeds before filing: a dollar for every $500 of price, with any remainder rounded up. Half stays with the county and half goes to the state.

Recording uses one statewide fee schedule. An ordinary instrument costs $26.00 through 15 pages plus $4.00 for each later page. A deed of trust costs $64.00 through 35 pages, and a certified copy runs $5.00 for page one and $2.00 per extra page.

The year's tax lien reaches back to the January listing date. Ask the closing attorney to confirm with Durham County that the bill is paid or arranged before funds move.

sections.h2: Zoning, tenants and estates before you sell
sections.html:
Durham's Unified Development Ordinance allows one accessory dwelling per lot. Heated floor area may reach 1,000 square feet for a single story and 1,200 square feet overall, with a different cap in the rural district. Check with planning staff on your lot before you promise a backyard unit to anyone.

  • Tenants: a monthly tenancy ends on a week's notice, and unpaid rent can end a lease 10 days after demand.
  • Foreclosure: heard by the superior court clerk, with later bids required to top the last by 5 percent, minimum $750.
  • Probate: an affidavit can settle an intestate estate of $20,000 or less after a 30 day wait, and no state estate tax applies to recent deaths.

Hand a buyer the lease and the permit file for any work on the house.

sections.h2: What to gather before you talk to buyers
sections.html:
A prepared seller closes faster, and the same papers help whether you list or take a cash offer. Collect the deed, your lender's payoff figure, the latest Durham County tax bill and any exemption approval. If the house is rented, add the lease and deposit records. Write down known repairs with an estimate beside each.

With cash, the buyer buys the house as it stands, so you skip repair negotiations after an inspection. With a listing, expect the buyer's lender to order an appraisal and expect a repair request or two. Compare the net from each route, not the headline price.

faqs.q: Which government values and taxes a Durham house?
faqs.a: Durham County does both, and every taxing body sets its own rate, so the final bill waits on those rates.

faqs.q: What is the next Durham County reappraisal date?
faqs.a: The county lists January 1, 2029. The current set of values began January 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Will a lowered value earn me a refund for past years?
faqs.a: No. State law makes a reduction effective for the year it is made and never retroactive.

faqs.q: How long does a Durham appeal review run?
faqs.a: The county gives a range of 30 to 120 days, depending on how many appeals your neighborhood produces.

faqs.q: Must I be home when a county appraiser visits?
faqs.a: Only if the appraiser needs to see the interior. Measurements are taken outside, and an appointment is set first if access is needed.
